items.title: Obi vows to end kidnappings, corruption
items.summary: Presidential candidate Peter Obi pledged to tackle kidnapping, corruption, and unemployment while promising to generate 10,000 megawatts of electricity and establish healthcare centres in every ward if elected in 2027. He emphasized moving Nigeria from a consumption-driven to production-based economy.
items.why: Obi's policy proposals address critical national challenges including security, power generation, and healthcare that directly impact citizens' daily lives.

items.title: Akpabio asks APC to shun violence
items.summary: Senate President Godswill Akpabio cautioned APC members against being provoked into violence by opposition supporters during 2027 election campaigns. He urged the ruling party to focus on winning votes through persuasion and highlighting government achievements rather than engaging in confrontations.
items.why: Akpabio's call for peaceful campaigning is crucial for maintaining electoral integrity and preventing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.title: NAFDAC destroys N100bn fake drugs, banned items
items.summary: NAFDAC destroyed fake, expired, and banned products valued at N100 billion, including counterfeit drugs, banned alcoholic beverages, and substandard cosmetics at a dumpsite in Ogun State. The agency uncovered illegal manufacturing operations in Lagos and arrested suspects for prosecution.
items.why: The destruction of counterfeit products protects public health and demonstrates NAFDAC's commitment to eliminating dangerous items from circulation.

items.title: Odegbami narrates near-death experience after attack
items.summary: Former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami survived an armed attack at his Abeokuta residence when three assailants broke into his home at 2:30am. Odegbami fought off the attackers with help from his driver and domestic worker, sustaining machete wounds before being hospitalized and discharged.
items.why: The attack on a prominent sports figure highlights rising security concerns in Nigeria and the need for improved personal safety measures.

items.title: FIFA President Infantino Inspects Ongoing Rehabilitation Work At Warri City Stadium
items.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino visited Delta State to inspect rehabilitation work at Warri City Stadium, which features modern facilities including a football pitch, athletics track, swimming pool, and media facilities. Infantino commended Nigeria's FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup victory and reaffirmed FIFA's commitment to grassroots football development across Africa.
items.why: The stadium upgrade demonstrates Nigeria's investment in sports infrastructure and positions the country as a hub for continental football development.

items.title: Osimhen, Onyeka return to club training after injuries
items.summary: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and midfielder Frank Onyeka have returned to training with their respective clubs following injury recoveries. Osimhen underwent knee surgery in Istanbul and is working toward match fitness, while Onyeka trained with Coventry City ahead of their Premier League fixture.
items.why: The return of key national team players strengthens Nigeria's squad depth ahead of upcoming Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers and international competitions.

items.title: Manufacturers, frozen food dealers groan as blackouts persist
items.summary: Manufacturers and frozen food dealers are suffering significant losses due to persistent power outages forcing reliance on expensive generators. A beverage company reported production capacity cuts of 40 percent and monthly energy costs of N130 million, with diesel expenditure between N16-20 million monthly.
items.why: The power crisis threatens business survival and economic growth, requiring urgent government intervention to stabilize electricity supply.

items.title: With new app, GTCO is giving its iconic 737 brand a second life
items.summary: Guaranty Trust Bank launched a new 737 mobile app that converts phone numbers into account numbers and combines payments, savings, lending, and virtual cards in a single interface. The move reflects the bank's strategy to compete with fintechs by offering a simplified, mobile-first platform for younger customers.
items.why: GTB's 737 app launch demonstrates traditional banks' adaptation to fintech competition and changing customer preferences for mobile-first banking.

items.title: Four Nigerian students win award
items.summary: Four Nigerian students from Destiny Christian Academy in Abuja placed second in the Middle Division category of the Future Problem Solving World Solutions Challenge with a project converting water hyacinth into biodegradable packaging. Their solution addresses water pollution while creating employment opportunities for local communities.
items.why: The achievement demonstrates Nigerian youth innovation and positions the country as a contributor to global solutions for environmental challenges.

items.title: Anthropic sets IPO price at $83 per share, targets $1.5trn valuation
items.summary: Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude chatbot, priced its IPO at $83 per share, raising $81.34 billion and becoming the world's largest IPO, surpassing SpaceX's previous record. The company achieved a $1.5 trillion valuation just five years after its 2021 founding by former OpenAI employees.
items.why: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO demonstrates explosive investor appetite for AI technology and marks a milestone in the global AI race.

items.title: 3,000 runners set for Capital City Race
items.summary: The third edition of the Capital City Race will hold in Lagos with 3,000 runners participating in a 10-kilometre event, offering N2 million in cash prizes. The race has grown from 1,000 participants in 2024 to full capacity this year, reflecting increasing interest in fitness and healthy living.
items.why: The growing participation in running events demonstrates rising public interest in health and wellness while contributing to Lagos's sports economy.

items.title: Brighton coach blames Nigeria for Yohanna blow
items.summary: Brighton manager Fabian Hürzeler blamed Nigeria's handling of winger Zadok Yohanna during U-23 Cup of Nations qualifiers for his re-injury, stating the player was not properly managed during international duty. Yohanna was forced off during Nigeria's match in Lubumbashi and will miss Brighton's upcoming fixture.
items.why: The incident highlights concerns about player welfare during international matches and the need for better coordination between clubs and national teams.

items.title: National anthem row: Youths ask Obi to apologise
items.summary: The Northern Youth Assembly gave presidential candidate Peter Obi a 72-hour ultimatum to apologize for the singing of Nigeria's former national anthem at an NDC gathering in Lagos. The group demanded clarification on his position regarding the current national anthem and commitment to national unity.
items.why: The controversy reflects sensitivities around national symbols and the need for political leaders to respect constitutional order during campaign activities.

items.title: Ekiti youths get grants to drive economy
items.summary: Sixty youths in Ekiti State received N100,000 grants each while 40 others secured internship opportunities at a youth summit focused on entrepreneurship and economic development. Speakers urged young people to become innovators and wealth creators rather than depend on politicians.
items.why: The initiative addresses youth unemployment and empowers young Nigerians to drive economic growth through entrepreneurship and innovation.

items.title: Olalere urges NSC to replicate judo success in gymnastics
items.summary: Lagos State Gymnastics Association chairperson Omowunmi Olalere urged the National Sports Commission to replicate the successful judo election process by resolving leadership disputes in the Gymnastics Federation. She commended the NSC's role in ensuring a credible judo transition.
items.why: Resolving governance issues in sports federations is essential for institutional stability and enabling athletes to compete at their best.
